sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in the column types, the link to the shared base and the portable UUID type.
sections.why: Likely reason: the three table classes below need these tools.
sections.watch_out: Keep the UUID alias consistent with the other model files.

sections.name: CapExModel
sections.title: Stored cost model per element
sections.what: Defines the table holding one fitted cost model per cost element, with its features, fit scores, error measures and diagnostics, linked to a project.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each fitted model so results can be reviewed and reused.
sections.watch_out: Coefficients and diagnostics are free-form JSON, so their keys are known only from the code that writes them.

sections.name: VarianceAnalysis
sections.title: Cost variance breakdown table
sections.what: Defines the table holding the baseline, one column per adjustment step, a full waterfall list and the unexplained remainder.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows where the cost gap comes from, one driver at a time.
sections.watch_out: The named adjustment columns and the waterfall list can disagree if only one of them is updated.

sections.name: OptimizationLever
sections.title: Cost reduction idea table
sections.what: Defines the table holding one named idea to cut cost, with its dollar and schedule impact, constraints, feasibility, risk and priority rank.
sections.why: Likely reason: turns the analysis into actions a user can review and rank.
sections.watch_out: Feasibility and risk are free text, not fixed choices, so values like high are only a convention.

summary: Defines three tables for capital cost models, cost variance breakdowns, and cost-reduction levers for a solar project.
purpose: Stores the fitted cost model for each cost element, the waterfall that explains how a project differs from a baseline, and ranked ideas to cut cost.
why: Likely reason: the benchmarking workflow must keep results so they can be reviewed and exported later.
how: 1) A CapEx model row stores the chosen features, the fitted coefficients and fit quality numbers. 2) A variance analysis row stores the baseline and each adjustment step. 3) A lever row links to a variance analysis and holds impact, constraints and priority.
inputs: Filled by the fitting and analysis code using project and comparator data.
outputs: Rows in the capex_models, variance_analyses and optimization_levers tables.
risks: Deleting a model also deletes its variance analyses, and deleting those deletes their levers. Money columns keep two decimals, so very precise values are rounded.
debug: If a stored cost looks wrong, compare it with the source comparator. If a model has no fit numbers, the fit step probably did not finish.
